title: Ship the `autonomous-ship` formula
description: `~/code/braynee/.beads/formulas/autonomous-ship.formula.toml` defines the 7-step gated DAG (scope→ci-harness→build→open-pr→ci-green→ship→verify-live) with all agnostic vars; `bd cook autonomous-ship --mode=runtime --var … --dry-run` exits 0 and emits all steps.
notes:
=== BUILD NOTE (cp-av7) — verified autonomous-ship formula ===
Create this file at: <repo>/.beads/formulas/autonomous-ship.formula.toml
Verified: formula parser accepts gh:run gate + `bd cook --dry-run` exit 0 (bd 1.0.3; source steveyegge/beads).
After writing, verify: bd cook autonomous-ship --mode=runtime --var name=x --var repo=o/r --var branch=feature/x --var deploy_target=vercel --dry-run

----- formula (autonomous-ship.formula.toml) -----
formula = "autonomous-ship"
version = 1
type    = "workflow"
description = "Scope -> wait CI green (gh:run) -> wait merge (gh:pr, human) -> deploy -> verify-live. Agnostic via vars."

[vars.name]
required = true
[vars.repo]
description = "owner/name — for gh + gates"
required = true
[vars.branch]
description = "feature branch to push"
required = true
[vars.ci_workflow]
description = "blocking CI workflow file/name (EXCLUDE the advisory Claude Code Review workflow)"
required = false
default  = "ci.yml"
[vars.gate_cmd]
description = "local verify cmd; empty = compose from lint+typecheck+test"
required = false
default  = ""
[vars.deploy_target]
description = "vercel | coolify-docker | pm2-vps | railway | npm-publish | electron-builder | plugin-cache"
required = true
[vars.secret_source]
description = "dotenv | infisical"
required = false
default  = "dotenv"

[[steps]]
id = "scope"
title = "Scope: {{name}}"
description = "One paragraph: deliverable, done-criteria, explicit non-goals."

[[steps]]
id = "ci-harness"
title = "Ensure CI exists: {{name}}"
needs = ["scope"]
description = "Confirm .github/workflows/{{ci_workflow}} runs lint+typecheck+test on pull_request; author it if absent. Do NOT count the advisory Claude review workflow as the gate."

[[steps]]
id = "build"
title = "Build: {{name}}"
needs = ["ci-harness"]
description = "Implement against scope. Run {{gate_cmd}} (or lint+typecheck+test if empty). Hard-stop on red."

[[steps]]
id = "open-pr"
title = "Open PR + wire gates: {{name}}"
needs = ["build"]
description = """
RUNTIME GATE WIRING (gh:pr cannot be declared statically — no PR number exists at pour):
1. git push -u origin {{branch}}
2. bd gate discover --branch {{branch}}            # fills the gh:run gate await_id
3. gh pr create --fill --base main --head {{branch}}
   NUM=$(gh pr view {{branch}} --json number --jq .number)
4. bd gate create --type=gh:pr --blocks <SHIP_ISSUE_ID> --await-id "$NUM" -r "wait human merge"
   (get <SHIP_ISSUE_ID> from `bd mol show` after pour)
5. Report PR URL + preview; bd gate add-waiter; then STOP. NEVER merge.
"""

[[steps]]
id = "ci-green"
title = "CI green: {{name}}"
needs = ["open-pr"]
  [steps.ci-green.gate]
  type     = "gh:run"
  await_id = "{{ci_workflow}}"
  timeout  = "2h"

[[steps]]
id = "ship"
title = "Ship: {{name}} -> {{deploy_target}}"
needs = ["ci-green"]
description = "Blocked by the runtime gh:pr gate until a HUMAN merges. Then deploy per {{deploy_target}}; secrets via {{secret_source}} (infisical run / .env). Presence-check CI secrets via `gh secret list` — never read values."

[[steps]]
id = "verify-live"
title = "Verify {{name}} live"
needs = ["ship"]
description = "Drive the deployed artifact and observe it works: agent-browser for web, smoke/curl/CLI otherwise. Behavior, not 'deploy succeeded'."
----- end formula -----

KEY DESIGN POINTS (do not lose):
- gh:run gate IS declared in the formula (ci-green). await_id="{{ci_workflow}}" is a workflow-name hint; `bd gate discover` (or `bd gate check` self-discovery) fills the run id. Empty await_id also works (discover matches by SHA/branch/time, --max-age 30m).
- gh:pr gate is NOT in the formula. open-pr creates it at runtime (step 4 above). SILENTLY never resolves if await_id is empty — always set the PR number.
- Ordering is safe: open-pr creates the gh:pr gate (blocking ship) before open-pr closes; ci-green needs open-pr, so ci-green cannot close until the gate already exists -> ship never goes briefly-ready.
- Human-merge policy (locked): open-pr reports PR + preview and STOPS. Autopilot never merges. Human merges -> gh:pr gate resolves on state==MERGED -> ship + verify-live proceed.
- Resolve gates: `bd gate discover --branch <b>` then `bd gate check --type=gh` (shells gh run view / gh pr view; gh authed as hamchowderr).
- Footgun: malformed `timeout` Go-duration is silently dropped — keep "2h"/"168h" valid.
Full context: PRD "Autonomous-Ship-Process" (Architecture) + memory reference_beads_gates_formula + "Canonical Stack Agent Command Reference".

title: [bug] qmd index split-brain: cache dir keyed off $HOME (empty on PowerShell/CC-hooks) -> two divergent indexes
description: qmd resolves its cache/index dir from process.env.HOME, NOT os.homedir(). Git Bash sets HOME=C:\Users\HamCh so qmd uses ~/.cache/qmd; PowerShell and Claude-Code-spawned hooks leave HOME empty, so qmd falls back to /tmp/.cache/qmd (C:\tmp). Result: two divergent indexes. braynee's hooks (empty HOME) maintain the /tmp index (all code collections, current) while manual Bash qmd AND braynee's own control/lock/stamp files (~/.cache) target a stale vault-only index. Searches return degraded/stale results and the embed backlog never clears in the index actually being queried. Affects every braynee user on Windows.
design: Pin HOME on every qmd spawn: env.HOME = process.env.HOME || os.homedir(). Two direct spawn sites: scripts/qmd-wrapper.mjs (spawnSync) and scripts/qmd-embed-runner.js (spawnSync). qmd-reindex.js already assumes os.homedir()/.cache/qmd for its control files, so this aligns qmd to match. Then migrate the richer index (currently /tmp) to canonical ~/.cache/qmd and delete the stray one. Deploy to live braynee cache.
acceptance_criteria: qmd status returns the SAME index path + vector counts whether invoked from Bash, PowerShell, or a CC hook. No /tmp/.cache/qmd (C:\tmp) index is created on fresh runs. The richer existing index is preserved (no re-embed from scratch). Fix deployed to the live braynee plugin cache and verified.
notes:
Found 2026-07-02 while debugging a RAM-thrash during a manual qmd embed. Evidence: ~/.cache had 62k vectors, vault-only, 2d stale; /tmp had 279k vectors, all collections, updated hourly. See vault memory reference_qmd_home_cache_split. User flagged super-high-priority — affects all users.
FIXED + DEPLOYED LOCALLY 2026-07-02. Pinned HOME=process.env.HOME||os.homedir() in scripts/qmd-wrapper.mjs (spawnOpts.env) and scripts/qmd-embed-runner.js (spawnSync env). Deployed both to live cache 2.1.11. Migrated rich index (279747 vectors, all collections) from stray C:\tmp\.cache\qmd to canonical ~/.cache/qmd; stale 62k index kept at index.sqlite.pre-migration-bak for rollback; deleted C:\tmp index. VERIFIED: Bash, PowerShell(empty HOME), and the live-cache wrapper all resolve to ~/.cache/qmd; no /tmp index recreated. REMAINING: git push to ship to other users (+version bump plugin.json/marketplace.json); 586 docs still pending embed (leave to scheduler or small chunked run).
close_reason: Fixed, deployed to live cache, verified end-to-end, and shipped to main as v2.1.12 (commit a6f3cb1). Pinned HOME on both qmd spawn points; migrated rich index to canonical ~/.cache/qmd; verified Bash + PowerShell + live-cache wrapper all resolve to one index with no /tmp regeneration.

title: Decide & migrate Infisical to per-project isolation (kill over-injection)

(B) Keep one project, one FOLDER per code project, inject with 'infisical run --path=/<project>' (drop --recursive); shared keys via imports from a /shared folder. Lighter migration but less true isolation.

title: Infisical: per-project secret isolation + auto-seed on project creation
description:
Three linked problems with how secrets are wired today:

1) OVER-INJECTION. Everything lives in ONE Infisical project (otaku-internal, id e56e0da5-6460-4bab-bdd6-2fd12ac5447b), organized folder-by-service, single 'dev' env, all --type=shared. Because of that layout, 'infisical run --recursive' is MANDATORY and injects EVERY key into EVERY project — most are irrelevant to the project being worked on. The user explicitly wants: working in a project should only inject that project's keys (plus a small genuinely-shared set).

2) UNDER-USE. We're likely glossing over Infisical capabilities that matter here: per-project isolation, scoped-path injection (--path=/X instead of --recursive), secret imports/references for genuinely-shared keys, machine identities (CI/agents), and multiple environments.

3) NO INFISICAL HOME ON CREATE. New projects don't get an Infisical home. Want: creating a project (braynee project-onboarder agent / 'project' pour formula) ALSO creates the matching Infisical project (or scoped folder) and seeds the expected API-key NAMES with dummy placeholders (YOUR_KEY_HERE) so the user fills real values later.

GOAL: move to a per-project secret structure so injection in a project brings only that project's keys + a small shared set, and wire project creation to bootstrap the Infisical side automatically.

CROSS-CUTTING FILES:
- braynee: agents/project-onboarder.md
- ~/.beads/formulas/project.formula.toml
- ~/.claude/skills/infisical/SKILL.md (top-level skill, not inside braynee)
- global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (Secrets section: the --recursive injection rule)
- vault notes: 2. Areas/Development/DevOps/Infisical/* (Folder Structure, Run & Inject, Imports & References, Secrets Standard & Migration Map)
- memory: reference_infisical_secrets, feedback-infisical-run-never-expose

See children for the decision, the seeding feature, and the convention update.

title: brainy: ensure-obsidian.js spawn leaves Windows zombie processes
description: ensure-obsidian.js calls spawn(exe, [], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }).unref() on Windows. Obsidian has a single-instance lock — second-instance spawns should message the first to focus, then exit cleanly. But the detached+no-stdio spawn pattern leaves the orphan running forever with no window (MainWindowHandle=0). Confirmed live: 5 Obsidian processes running, 1 with visible window (PID 32600 from 09:46), 1 orphan zombie (PID 3660 from 14:59 — when this Claude Code session started). Windows routes user taskbar clicks to the most recent process, which is the windowless zombie — clicks silently fail. Fix: on Windows use execSync('start "" "<exe>"') which delegates to the Windows shell and handles single-instance correctly. Test by killing existing zombies, running the hook, and verifying only one process remains.

description: ~12 orphan per-project dolt sql-servers (high random ports, --loglevel=warning) are running alongside the shared server (127.0.0.1:3308). SCAN RESULTS (2026-06-06, read-only): 122 beads projects in ~/code. 28 shared (port 3308). 94 per-project. Only 12 have a LIVE orphan server right now (port->project): 50738 alchemist-template, 50755 brokerboard, 50876 sophon, 64820 sophon-sdk-typescript, 55716 ag-ui, 55778 aitable-mcp, 55826 apps-sdk-audit, 55835 apps-sdk-nasa, 55848 arscontexta, 55857 beta-testers-bot, 55868 bika-mcp, 57878 cc-challenge. Other 82 per-project projects have a stale .beads/dolt-server.port but no running server. Config knob = dolt.shared-server: true in .beads/config.yaml; port in .beads/dolt-server.port. EDGE: sophon-extension has port 3308 but shared-server not set (verify). Projects with no port file (no-db/uninit): beads, beads-sdk, cc-challenge-mcp, mastra-base/-descript/-ncat/-rag/-voice, sophon-landing, storycraft. PLAN: pilot-migrate ONE of the 12 (bd init --shared-server --external), verify issue count preserved + old server stoppable, then batch the rest.
PILOT FINDING (2026-06-06): NO clean supported 'migrate existing project to shared server' command in bd 1.0.4. bd init --shared-server is an IDENTITY re-init (init-safety: mints/re-inits project_id, needs --reinit-local over existing data) — too risky to bulk-run on 94 repos (could change prefixes/IDs). bd dolt set only covers database/host/port/user/data-dir, no shared-server toggle. Config-flip (hand-edit dolt.shared-server:true + port 3308) relies on undocumented auto-import and risks shared-DB-name collisions (DB named by issue prefix). The 28 already-shared projects were almost certainly bd init --shared-server at CREATION, not migrated. CONCLUSION: bulk consolidation is NOT cleanly supported; do not hack it across repos. Orphans are harmless idle RAM, created on-demand. RECOMMEND: either leave them, or gracefully 'bd dolt stop -C <dir>' the 12 running ones (safe flush, they respawn on next use). Revisit true consolidation only if bd ships a supported migrate path. alchemist-template pilot left UNCHANGED.

title: Harden MEMORY.md index against 25KB startup-load overflow
description: The global-brain design (autoMemoryDirectory -> single vault dir) pools every project's memory into one MEMORY.md index. CC auto-loads only the first 200 lines / 25KB at session start; the index has grown to 25.5KB and now truncates. Root causes: (1) index lines built from frontmatter 'description' are not length-capped (some 300+ chars); (2) cross-section duplicate entries (same file linked under both Feedback and References). Fix with permanent guards so it cannot recur: #1 truncate description to 180 chars in syncMemoryIndex; #2 dedupe one-file-one-line per type-section in resyncAllMemoryNotes; #3 health.py tripwire warning above ~22KB; #4 run improved resync once as one-time cleanup; #5 update hooks/lib/memory-index tests. No memory files are modified, only the MEMORY.md index is regenerated from existing frontmatter (mechanical, no semantic reading).
notes: Implemented + verified. Root cause deeper than expected: memory files use TWO frontmatter shapes (flat type: newer; nested metadata:>type: older). parseFrontmatter read only flat keys, so 19 nested-type files lost type, defaulted to References, and resync added a SECOND entry beside the writer's correct one = the cross-section duplicates. Fixes: (1) parseFrontmatter reads nested metadata.type (top-level wins); (2) buildIndexLine/syncMemoryIndex truncate desc to MAX_DESC_LEN=180; (3) resyncAllMemoryNotes rewritten to REGENERATE MEMORY.md from frontmatter (one line/file, correct section, sorted, truncated, idempotent) = also the one-time cleanup; (4) health.py warns when MEMORY.md>=22KB; (5) new hooks/lib/memory-index.test.js (29 assertions). One-time cleanup ran: 25.9KB/122 lines -> 18.8KB/95 lines, 85 files deduped+rehomed. Self-test 128/128. NOT committed (on master; awaiting branch+commit).

description:

  [brainy] Hook error in check-git-init: git init failed: 'git' is not recognized as an internal or external command

Root cause: check-git-init.js tryGitInit() (line 15) runs `execSync('git init -b main')` with NO check that git exists / is on PATH. When git is absent, execSync throws ENOENT/'not recognized'; the catch turns it into result.ok=false and the hook then logs `log.error(HOOK, git init failed: ...)` and writes a "git init failed" message — surfacing a confusing hook ERROR rather than the actionable "install git" guidance.

DISTINCT from the ~/code gate fix (that work is done): this is a git-PRESENCE robustness gap. R-1-adjacent — empirical proof that git is an unguarded hard assumption (see cp-jt8 / R-1, where git was made a required setup dependency with cross-platform install guidance). check-git-init.js should mirror check-beads-init.js: detect git absence FIRST (e.g. `git --version` probe or distinguish ENOENT/'not recognized' from a real init error), and on absence emit the R-1-style install guidance (winget/brew/apt) and exit 0 cleanly — NOT attempt `git init` and report a failure/throw a hook error.

References: R-1, cp-jt8 (git as required setup dependency). Track only; do NOT fix in PR #12 — separate non-blocking follow-up.
close_reason: Added isGitOnPath() probe (mirrors check-beads-init.js Step 1) + git-absence guard BEFORE any init attempt in check-git-init.js. title: qmd: embed-only persistent HTTP MCP daemon for fast vector search (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED — user chose this direction (option 2) on 2026-05-27 but to revisit later, not build now.

PROBLEM: vector search (vsearch/query) costs 18-60s per call because each qmd CLI invocation cold-starts (loads model + inits Vulkan). Also stdio MCP servers do NOT auto-reconnect (CC only auto-reconnects HTTP/SSE) — qmd dropped this session under memory pressure and needed manual /mcp.

PLAN (embed-only, ~0.5-0.7GB resident — NOT the full 3GB; skip the 1.2GB expansion + 0.6GB rerank by avoiding hybrid query / using vsearch):
1. Run qmd as HTTP daemon: 'qmd mcp --http --daemon' (verify exact --http host/port flags at impl time; generic help only notes they exist).
2. Repoint qmd MCP registration in ~/.claude.json (+ ~/.claude/settings.json) from stdio command -> HTTP url. User-scoped so it covers all sessions incl --plugin-dir sandboxes.
3. braynee SessionStart hook with async:true that idempotently ensures the daemon is running (single-flight, windowsHide, self-gating, no duplicate spawns — mirror qmd-embed-runner's lock pattern). Hook can't reconnect the MCP link (impossible) but CAN keep the server process alive; CC's HTTP transport then auto-reconnects to it.

BENEFITS: persistent model = no per-query cold start; HTTP transport = CC auto-reconnect; async hook = auto-start without a Windows startup task.
TRADEOFF: ~0.5GB standing RAM (acceptable vs the full 3GB; machine is 16GB and hit swap during heavy embed today).
CONTEXT: node-llama-cpp 3.18.1, Vulkan on Intel iGPU already in use (not a CPU-thread issue). Models: embed gemma-300M Q8 314MB, rerank qwen3-0.6B 610MB, expansion 1.7B 1.2GB. Verify daemon RAM empirically before committing.
design: Run qmd as a persistent embed-only HTTP MCP daemon (~0.5-0.7GB resident) rather than the full 3GB stack — skip the 1.2GB expansion + 0.6GB rerank by using vsearch over hybrid query. HTTP transport is chosen over stdio because CC only auto-reconnects HTTP/SSE (stdio dropped under memory pressure this session). An async, single-flight SessionStart hook (windowsHide, mirrors qmd-embed-runner lock) keeps the daemon alive; trade-off is ~0.5GB standing RAM, acceptable vs 3GB on a 16GB machine that hit swap.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] qmd runs as a persistent HTTP MCP daemon so vector queries incur no per-call cold start
- [ ] The qmd MCP registration uses the HTTP URL (user-scoped), letting CC auto-reconnect after a drop
- [ ] A SessionStart hook idempotently keeps the daemon alive without spawning duplicates
- [ ] Standing daemon RAM is empirically verified to stay near the embed-only ~0.5-0.7GB target
